name: AeWF Television Championship
caption: A championship billed under a rival promotion's own initials but defended and held exclusively on IWE's own broadcasts in this collection's holdings.
epitaph: A career-vs-title match settled its only documented change of hands, ending the defending champion's own in-ring career on the promotion's comeback special.
notes: Billed throughout this document as the "AeWF Television Championship"; no document in this collection's holdings ties it to the wholly unrelated held federation carrying the same initials (a 1990s European promotion). Recorded here, under the promotion whose own card is the only one in this collection to defend it, exactly as billed.

name: IWE World Tag Team Championship
caption: The promotion's own tag team championship, billed as newly reinstated for a four-way elimination match on the comeback special.
epitaph: Its own former champions fell in the very tournament that crowned their successors, on the promotion's comeback special.
notes: Billed as "newly reinstated" ahead of the four-way match that crowned Enemies of the State; the previous champions, God's Justice, are named only in the broadcast's own commentary, with no document surviving in the held record to date their own reign.

name: IWE Intercontinental Championship
caption: Abolished for four years before the promotion's comeback special crowned a new champion in a bloody two-out-of-three-falls match.
epitaph: Vacant for four years, the title was finally awarded after a cage match climax that saw one combatant deliberately set his own opponent's face on fire.
notes: The broadcast's own commentary states the title "had been abolished for the past four years" before this card; no prior holder is named in this collection's holdings.

name: IWE World Heavyweight Championship
caption: The promotion's top title, vacant since a 1999 closure the broadcast itself declines to elaborate on, awarded in a three-way main event marred by hired interference.
epitaph: Vacant since the federation's own prior closure in 1999, the title was awarded in a three-way main event decided by a betrayed betrayal.
notes: The broadcast's own commentary states "the IWE was last held in 1999," without naming the prior champion, before cutting itself off ("Names aren't necessary"). A wholly unrelated held federation's own wrestler biography independently attests an earlier IWE World Title reign for a wrestler named Chris Hopper, won from a wrestler named Kame at a card called "Survival of the Fittest," with Hopper still champion when the league closed — the flashback footage on this card's own broadcast replays that exact same title-winning sequence. That reign is not structured in this record: its own event is not a document held in the held record, only a third-party mention in another wing's biography page, so no show record exists here to anchor it.
